canonical_topic: Physical control of nuclear reaction speed (fuel shape and control rods)
definition: Beyond enrichment level, a reactor's fuel geometry and graphite control rods are used to physically govern how fast the fission chain reaction proceeds.
core_idea: Fuel shaped as a flat sheet (rather than a compact ball) lets more radiation escape and slows the reaction, while graphite control rods can be inserted to absorb radiation and further throttle fission speed — a power plant wants slow/controlled fission, a weapon wants fast/maximal fission.
key_points: A weapon wants fuel shaped into a ball to maximize chain-reaction speed.
A power plant wants fuel shaped into a flat sheet so energy escapes from the top and bottom, reducing chain-reaction speed.
Graphite control rods fine-tune fission speed by absorbing radiation before it can trigger fission in another atom.
Control rods can be inserted into the reactor chamber to slow down the reaction.
relationships: Fuel shape and control rods are complementary, independent levers (along with enrichment %) for managing reaction speed.
caveats: Reaction speed control isn't just about enrichment percentage — physical fuel geometry and control rods are separate, additional mechanisms.
